meta.title: Energy-Based Transformers for Symbolic Music
meta.subtitle: Listening examples: continuation and attribute steering with an Energy-Based Transformer (EBT), compared with GPT-2 and Llama baselines.
meta.author: Rebecca Ceccatelli
meta.disclaimer: These are selected examples. All clips come from the final evaluation runs: frozen final checkpoints, per tokenizer the same 16 validation prompts for every model and method, 256 generated tokens, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.9. Within each example every system gets the same prompt and its first sample (no per-system cherry-picking). Clips tagged PLACEHOLDER are stand-ins for outputs that don't exist yet. The aggregate results are in the thesis.

sections.title: Unguided Generation
sections.intro: Each model gets the same short prompt (shaded) and continues it, with no control. All models are small and trained on GigaMIDI, once per tokenizer. REMI encodes music as bar/position/pitch/velocity/duration tokens; Anticipation encodes (time, duration, note) triplets. The EBT generates each token by minimising a learned energy with a few gradient steps; Llama and GPT-2 are standard next-token predictors.

sections.title: Single-Attribute Control
sections.intro: With a small regressor that predicts a musical attribute, generation can be steered toward a target without retraining. Each tab compares the baselines for autoregressive models (Tilt, Best-of-16 and PPLM, all on Llama) with the EBT, where the regressor's error is added to the energy it already minimises and a guidance strength sets how hard it pushes. Targets are given in standard deviations (SD) of the corpus, relative to the prompt's own unguided level.

blocks.title: What do “SD” and “strength” mean?
blocks.text: SD (the target) = where you ask the music to go: “a bit louder” (+1 SD) or “much louder” (+2 SD); minus means the opposite direction. SD stands for standard deviation, how much loudness, note length or pitch usually varies between pieces.Strength (low / medium / high) = how hard the model is pushed to get there: how insistently you ask, not what you ask for.Think of throwing a ball at a target: the SD is where you aim, the strength is how hard you throw. Too soft and it falls short; too hard and it flies past and goes wild, which is what “Pushing Too Hard” shows.

sections.title: Combined Control
sections.intro: Two attributes steered at once, loudness and note length, in all four direction combinations (REMI). The EBT simply adds one regressor energy per attribute; PPLM sums the two regressors' gradients, best-of-N the two distances, and tilting chains two tilts. Every tab uses the same prompt, so the unguided versions are identical and the tabs can be compared directly.

sections.title: Pushing Too Hard
sections.intro: Guidance strength is a trade-off. Past the recommended strength, strong EBT guidance flattens the model's choice among attribute values: the target is reached by scattering near-random notes. Harsh dissonance (share of simultaneous note pairs a semitone, major seventh or tritone apart) rises to the level of uniformly random notes, about 0.25.
